site.notes: Found by First Read on the address '375 Glen Drive': the City's property address '375 Glen Drive, Vancouver, BC (City of Vancouver property address, Strathcona)'. Zoning district CD-1 (819) (CD-1 by-law 819) from the City's zoning districts dataset at that point. A CD-1 district has no general schedule: its limits are in CD-1 by-law No. 819. Lot area 1,941.7 m² from the parcel polygon (4 vertices, not a rectangle: the frontage and depth are an equivalent rectangle with the same area); frontage taken as the side along Glen Drive from OpenStreetMap, 36.2 m away. A corner lot: E Hastings St also runs beside it, 33.3 m from the centre. The frontage is taken on Glen Drive (34.6 m); the front could instead be the 56.1 m side on E Hastings St Confirm which side is the front: it sets the yards, the envelope and the massing. Four sides but not square-cornered (86% of its 60.4 x 37.2 m bounding rectangle), 1,942 m2. The massing uses the polygon itself: the setback envelope follows the lot lines and the plate is the largest rectangle inside it. Transit-oriented area, the Community Vision map, water and sewer, trees and the owner are not in these datasets: answer them, or leave them 'not sure'. Answers added by hand for the 17 Nov 2026 demonstration: owner City of Vancouver (Daily Hive, 17 Feb 2021); not a former Community Vision area (the site is inside the Downtown Eastside Plan area; confirm on the City's map); transit-oriented area No (no SkyTrain station within 800 m; confirm on the City's TOA map); frequent bus stop Yes (E Hastings St; confirm against TransLink's frequent transit network). Site area set by hand to 2,134.4 m2: the draft CD-1 by-law (s.5.1) says the floor space ratio must be computed on the site as it was at the rezoning application, before any dedications. The City's parcel today is 1,941.7 m2, the figure the lookup found; the referral report requires a 5 m dedication to CN Rail along the western property line, which accounts for the difference. The parcel polygon is today's, so the massing warns that it is smaller than the recorded area. The report gives the lot as about 50 m on Hastings St and 37 m on Glen Drive, with no trees on the site or the street, and Hastings St as Frequent Transit Network. area_plan set by hand to downtown_eastside: the referral report places the site in the Hastings East sub-area of the Downtown Eastside Plan. front_face set by hand to E Hastings St (17 Nov 2026): the referral report gives the lot as about 50 m on Hastings St and 37 m on Glen Drive, the rezoning address is 1015 East Hastings St, and the social housing wing and the shelter are entered from Hastings; fronted on Glen Drive the setbacks leave a plate box only 30 m wide, too short for a double-loaded bar.

option.name: 375 Glen Drive, as referred to public hearing (rezoned as 1015 East Hastings St; referral report, 5 Jan 2021): 15 and 13 storeys, 163 homes, an 80-bed shelter
option.proponent: BC Housing with the Vancouver Aboriginal Friendship Centre Society, on City land
option.rezoning_path: M-1 to CD-1 (819) under the Downtown Eastside Plan
option.notes: From the referral report: a 15-storey wing on the lane (110 social housing homes, 25 of them supportive) and a 13-storey wing on Glen Drive (53 secured market rental homes); 14,729 m2 at FSR 6.90 on 2,134.4 m2; height to 51.0 m at the parapet above the rooftop amenity; 10 ft floor to floor; 59 vehicle and 308 bicycle spaces; about 36 trees proposed; an 80-bed shelter and a 423 m2 social enterprise; a Housing Agreement for the longer of 99 years and the life of the building; the social housing owned by BC Housing. Unit mix: the 25 supportive homes are 21 studios and 4 one-bedrooms (report); the 85 other social homes 15/35/30/5 and the 53 market rentals 15/33/5 (the application as reported by Daily Hive); the report confirms 35 two-bedroom and 5 three-bedroom homes in all. Rents: a third of the 110 social homes at the shelter rate (including all 25 supportive), a third geared to income up to HILs, a third at the low end of market; entered as 37/37/36, the rounding is assumed, and the 53 market rentals are added to the market tier. Assumptions, not from the report: the floor area is not split between residential and the shelter, so both are left blank; the setbacks are placeholders for the massing; the 15 storeys are drawn as one block although the Glen Drive wing is 13; the Community Housing Fund is the nearest program in the rule stack (the report says the partners were still seeking senior government contributions); tenure is entered as social housing although 53 of the 163 homes are market rental. The building permit (BP-2021-05332, full construction 18 Oct 2023) differs: 16 storeys (15 under the Zoning and Development By-law), 25 supportive + 87 affordable + 56 market rental + 2 townhouses = 170 homes, $55,000,000. Beds (24 Nov 2026): the 80-bed shelter the referral report names is entered as beds, so the memo reads it as a shelter part of the building; its floor area is still not split out.
